title: Platform Integrator Pocket Guidance — QuickRef (Draft)
content:
Context / purpose:
This is a one-page (plus notes) quick reference for SEs and platform integrators during technical discovery and pilot kickoff with platform/integration engineering teams. Goal: give a compact, evidence-backed script and checklist so sellers can rapidly qualify latency/cost/ops constraints and propose a minimally invasive pilot that demonstrates value while minimizing infra risk.

Audience:
- Platform engineering leads, integration architects, and SREs
- SEs and account execs running a technical discovery or pilot kickoff

How to use this doc (tl;dr):
- 60s opener: use the 3-line pitch and the quick ask
- 5–10 min qualification: run the technical qual checklist and capture answers in the call notes template (below)
- Pilot proposal: use suggested minimal config and success metrics. Offer fallback patterns if constraints exist.

Three-line opener (script):
"Redwood Inference provides a predictable inference runtime you can run hosted, on dedicated capacity, or inside your VPC. For a pilot, we focus on proving latency and cost for your critical route with an isolated dataset and can fail over to a cheaper quantized model if needed. Can I ask a few questions about your traffic profile and security needs?"

Quick ask (during qualification):
"If this looks promising we can stand up a two-week pilot that uses a single endpoint and a tiny sample dataset. We’ll measure 95th-p latency, tokens-per-second throughput, and per-token cost. Pilot requires one engineering contact and access to a test service account or a private VPC peering window (if you want on-prem)."

Technical qualification checklist (5–10 minutes):
- Workload shape: typical request size (input tokens) and max generation length? (notes)
- Traffic profile: concurrent requests (p95 rps), burst behaviour, predictable windows?
- Latency SLOs: target p50/p95/p99 and acceptable tail?
- Cost priority: tighter latency vs lower cost? (tradeoff preference)
- Data security: can you share a masked sample? Do you need VPC/private deployment and KMS/HSM keys?
- Model constraints: must we pin to a model family, or can we test lighter quantized variants?
- Integration touchpoints: single API call, async jobs, streaming? Webhook callbacks?
- Observability needs: do you need token-level cost breakdowns, per-request traces, or custom audit logs?
- Ops requirements: SLA, runbook for degraded performance, and an escalation contact?
- Regulatory/compliance: data residency, retention, encryption at rest/in transit?

Notes template (SE copy/paste):
- request_shape: __tokens_in__/__max_gen__
- traffic_profile: p95_rps=__, burst=__, concurrency=__
- latency_slo: p50=__, p95=__, p99=__
- pilot_window: planned_start=__, duration=__
- security: VPC_required=Y/N, KMS=Y/N, audit_logs=Y/N
- integration: sync/async/streaming, payload_size_bytes=__
- success_metrics: latency_target=__, cost_target=__, quality_bench=__ (eval prompt set)
- se_contact / eng_contact: name / email

Minimal pilot proposal (low-friction, 2-week):
- Scope: 1 critical route (single endpoint) + masked test dataset (~200–500 snippets)
- Deployment: Hosted API w/ reserved burst capacity OR Private deployment (VPC) if required by security
- Config: quantization profile suggestion: int8-ggml or 4-bit group-quant for cost-sensitive pilots; pin model family to avoid surprises
- Observability: short token-level retention (7 days), 95th-latency dashboard preconfigured
- Rollout: start small (1 rps), run synthetic load + real traffic ramp to target p95 for 48h
- Success: meet p95 latency target and stay under projected per-token cost threshold for 48h window; quality measured against sample prompt suite (F1/accuracy/qual score)

Fallback & mitigation scripts (language for SEs):
- If platform says "latency is critical and we can’t use hosted": "We can run Private (VPC) or Dedicated capacity and co-locate in your region. For the pilot we’ll propose a small Dedicated pool with autoscaling and isolated KV cache to keep tail latency predictable."
- If they say "cost is the primary constraint": "We’ll test a quantized model family and enable prefix/KV caching; we’ll run a short job to measure effective tokens-per-dollar and tune batch sizes. If quality drops, we’ll show top-k tradeoffs and a fast fallback to a higher-fidelity variant for critical routes only."
- If they ask "what if we lose model parity": "We’ll run an eval harness up front comparing your current model outputs vs Redwood variants on your prompt set — provide evaluation artifacts and a rollback policy for the pilot."

Redwood-specific quick config examples (shareable on call):
- API example (minimal):
POST /v1/generate
headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
body: {"model":"redwood-v1-mini","input":"<masked-prompt>","max_tokens":128,"stream":false}
(Explain: model family, max_tokens, stream flag)

- Suggested pilot settings (ops):
-- start-concurrency: 1 rps
-- ramp: +1 rps per 30m until target p95 observed
-- batch window: platform-managed auto-batching (we’ll recommend parameters after initial trace)

Quality checks (short eval to run before/after):
- 200 prompt samples held-out; compare top-1 exact-match and two human-review snippets for high-value routes
- Collect qualitative flags: hallucination, sensitive content, tone/length issues

Common objections (and lines):
- "We can’t share data" -> "We can work with synthetically masked samples or run entirely in VPC/on-prem with customer-managed KMS."
- "We need strict tail latency guarantees" -> "We’ll propose Dedicated pool with minimum instance reservation and autoscale constraints; we can also route high-priority traffic to a lower-latency variant."
- "How do you measure cost?" -> "We provide token-level accounting, and we’ll run a short cost-projection during the pilot once we capture tokens/second and cache hit rates."

Ops handoff checklist (post-pilot if we proceed):
- Exported perf traces and cost report (p95/p99, tokens-per-second, cost/projection)
- Runbook: degradation detection, auto-fallback policy, contact list
- Recommended long-term config: dedicated vs reserved-hosted, model variants to keep, quantization profile

Open questions (for internal follow-up):
- Do we want a pre-built SE slide with a simple two-axis chart mapping latency vs cost for our top 4 verified model variants? (I think yes — action for Evan)
- Default kernel/quantization recommendation to show during calls for each model family (Sofia owns a short table)
- Handoff template into Solutions Eng / Professional Services for VPC onboarding (Rohit follow-up)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the pilot as non-invasive as possible — customers hate long infra changes for pilots.
- Offer synthetic data path as a default to reduce legal friction early.
- Make sure SEs capture an actual latency SLO number on the first call — if they say "low" follow up with examples (e.g., 100ms p95).
- If customer wants to test at scale, do a short paid proof (charge nominally) so infra cost is not buried.

Attachments to create (next steps):
- one-pager: "Pilot in 10 minutes" (single sheet with config + success metrics) [TODO Evan]
- 2-slide "latency vs cost" model mapping for quick share [TODO Sofia]
- VPC onboarding checklist (with estimated times) [TODO Rohit]

Links & references:
- Internal eval harness notes: CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-1048
- Example JIRA for pilot onboarding: JIRA-PLT-789

End of doc — this is intentionally short and conversational. Use as a call script + capture template.

-- Maya
